youtube_title: Tippecanoe Place: the Studebaker mansion in South Bend, and the voices people report
body: Voices. Pictures swinging on the walls. That's what people have reported inside Tippecanoe Place, the Studebaker mansion in South Bend. Wagon maker Clem Studebaker had the 40-room stone mansion built, and it was finished in 1889. That same year, fire burned the roof and gutted much of the inside, but the stone walls survived. It was restored within a year. Clem died in 1901. In World War 2 the house was a Red Cross headquarters, and later a school for disabled children. In 1980 it became a restaurant, and legend says some of the Studebakers never left. The restaurant closed in January 2026. The mansion is private: please view it from the road. 👻 Comment your town, and it could be next! #SouthBend #Studebaker #TippecanoePlace #Indiana #Haunted #LaPorteAfterDark
